parties:
Anu Bala ------- Petitioner.
Vs.
Upazila Nirbahi Officer, Perojpur and Others ------- Opposite-Party.
full_judgment:
Anwarul Hoque Chowdhury, J.: This is an application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and is directed against the judgement and order dated 23.7.90 passed by the District Judge, Perojpor, in Title Appeal No. 67 of 1990 allowing an application for condonation under section 5 of the Limitation Act. 

 4. The defendant Government contested the suit by filing written statement stating, inter alia, that the suit is barred by limitation, and hit under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. It is the case of the Government that Krishna Kanta did not die in this country but died in India and the plaintiff petitioner did not get the property and the property was rightly included in the vested property, the plaintiff had got no right and possession. After it is declared vested property Abdus Sobhan and others had been given lease of the property and they are in possession and that even the brother of Krishna Kanta, Hiralal took lease of some portion of the said as vested property and he is in possession of his leased out property. 

 5. The Court below on a careful consideration of the pleadings of the parties and the evidence on record decreed the suit vide judgment and order dated 30.8.89 and the decree was signed on 7.6.89 and on 5.5.90 the opposite party Nos. 1 to 3 namely, the Custodian of Vested Property and others filed Title Appeal No. 67 of 1990 in the Court of District Judge, Perojpur, with an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation. It was heard by the District Judge, Perojpur who by his order dated 3.7.90 condoned the delay. 

 9. We have gone through the decision, under report and we find that a Division Bench of this Court in condoning the delay in filing the Title Appeal No. 127 of 1988 observed that though the law of limitation makes no distinction between a private person and Government except in certain provision like Article 149 of the Limitation Act, yet in dealing with an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act, the fact would remain that the private individual had to make up their own mind only and had to arrange his own fund and is normally presumed to be aware of the facts and aspects of the case while in the case of Government public interest has to be duly considered that the case of the Government in such matters various authorities, formalities and completions including allocation of budget and sanction of fund by the Ministry are involved and as such the Government required long time in making the decision then in processing the matter for acting on it. If on behalf of the Government a reasonable explanation for delay in relevant matters is given for filing the appeal there is no reason why such reasonable explanation should not be accepted. 

 11. That being the legal position in case of delay in filing an appeal by the Government or on behalf of the Government some considerations in appropriate circumstances may, therefore, be extended to the Government appearing as a litigant and though the Government is not above the law of limitation, yet the Government might have reasons and reasonable cause of delay which may not always be a ground for delay in case of individual because an individual is to decide himself as to whether to file an appeal or not, may be, after consulting one lawyer. he is to arrange the fund needed as legal cost. He is thus expected to move more quickly than the Government, who is rather a slow moving juristic person. Legislature having acknowledged that fact provided 60 years limitation in all suits filed by the Government or on behalf of the Government under Article 149 of the Limitation Act, when for private individuals the limitation in most suits are 3 years. In case of filing of appeals no such extension is given to the Government and the State hence needs to go by the limitation applicable to all, but if it is delayed, some consideration need be allowed to the Government considering the fact that even in case of filing of appeals, the Government remains a slow moving juristic person all the same.
